annotations.title: Subtitle files from words with times

description: Use it when the user wants an SRT, VTT or ASS subtitle file for a video. Writes subtitle files from words with times the user already has, and changes no video: captions.srt and captions.vtt, lines of up to 42 characters for any player or place that takes a captions file, captions.ass with the font, the colors and the place, laid out for the frame of the video given (else a phone's for tiktok, reels or shorts, a square for square alone, and 16:9 for the rest), and words.json, captions.json and CAPTIONS.md, which the result shows with how fast the captions read. The words are a speech-to-text JSON, an SRT or WebVTT file, or a demo's steps file, whose step notes become the captions; without video, a demo's captions end where its steps file says the video does. To burn the captions into the video, use caption_video instead. The captions playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (easycaptionkit 0.1.5, on this machine.)

box.description: A dark box behind the words in captions.ass instead of an outline.

brand.description: A brand kit, its folder or brand.json, for captions.ass's highlight color and font. make_brand_kit makes one.

font.description: A font family for captions.ass, like Inter.

fonts.description: A font kit, its folder or fonts.css, for captions.ass's font. make_font_kit makes one.

for.description: The places the video goes to, whose free space captions.ass keeps to (default: the places of the video's shape, or of the frame laid out).

highlight.description: The spoken word's color in captions.ass, like #ffd23f.

lines.description: Lines a caption may take, 1 to 3 (default 2).

max_chars.description: Characters a line of captions.srt and captions.vtt may take, 8 to 80 (default 42); captions.ass cuts its lines to what fits across its frame.

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: <words-folder>/easycaptionkit-subtitles-<words-name>, where <words-name> is the name of words without its extension and <words-folder> is the folder words is in. A run replaces the files an earlier run of this kit left there, so give each version its own out_dir.

position.description: Where in the free space captions.ass puts them (default bottom).

size.description: The letters' size in captions.ass, in percent of a phone's width or of the frame's short side, 2 to 20 (default 6.5, or 9.5 for the word style).

style.description: How captions.ass shows them: karaoke lights the word being spoken (default karaoke), line shows whole captions, word one word at a time.

video.description: The video the subtitles are for, read for its size and length only.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

words.description: The words and their times: a speech-to-text JSON, an SRT or WebVTT file, a demo's steps.json, or the words.json of an earlier run with a misheard word fixed by hand.

name: make_subtitles

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.

title: Subtitle files from words with times
